title: Stitch Runner: phased migration weave for VPC/on-prem upgrades, LTS awareness & rollout gates
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Build a resilient, audit-able upgrade/migration orchestrator ("Stitch Runner") for Redwood Private that coordinates component-level upgrades, schema migrations, and configuration rollouts across VPC and on-prem clusters. Stitch Runner must: 1) understand LTS channel pins and version compatibility matrix, 2) provide cohorted canary and staged rollouts with configurable gates (health, latency, error budgets, SLO regressions), 3) support transactional and non-blocking data migrations with pause/resume and automatic rollback policies, 4) emit detailed audit events and integrate with KMS/HSM-backed secrets for private control planes, and 5) include preflight probes, drift detection, and a dry-run simulation mode for customer signoff. Deliverables: orchestration service and CRDs/hooks for private control plane, CLI for operators, integrations for Console rollouts UI and telemetry, end-to-end tests and runbooks.
comments: 2026-02-21: Kickoff with Release Eng, Infra, and Customer Success. Agreed success criteria: zero-downtime upgrade for 90% small clusters, clear rollback on failure, and observable migration steps.
2026-02-22: Design review -- prefer cohort-by-tenant approach (region/cohort size configurable) over single-node canary to reduce blast radius. Action: prototype cohort controller (Arjun).

2026-02-25: Trade-off discussion: two-phase DB migrations (online + backfill) vs transactional in-place. Decided to support both patterns; provide migration policy DSL for operators to pick per release.
2026-02-28: PoC: preflight compatibility checks running in a kube Job, validating release manifest, model artifacts, kernel profile. Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/stitch-runner/pull/12
2026-03-03: Security sync: KMS integration approach approved (envelope encryption with customer-managed keys). Need security review for CLI key use-case. Ticket added for HSM test harness.

2026-03-07: Telemetry plan approved: emit per-step events to Console (trace_id, step, duration, status). Estimate 0.5 token-cost per event. Backend changes tracked in https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/423

2026-03-11: Implementation update: coordinator API v1 implemented; basic cohort scheduling and rollback hooks wired. Integration tests failing intermittently on large cluster simulation (flaky due to resource quotas). Investigating with infra team.
2026-03-12: PM feedback (Lina Zhou): add explicit 'customer opt-in' flag for major migrations and provide a signed preflight report for compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator can schedule a staged rollout across N cohorts with configurable gate checks (health, latency, error-rate)
A release pinned to an LTS channel refuses incompatible component upgrades and surfaces suggested compatibility fixes
CLI and Console show a signed preflight report and dry-run output for customers
Automatic rollback triggers on gate failures and leaves a clear audit trail with actionable diagnostics
Migration policies support both transactional (blocking) and online (non-blocking + backfill) patterns
End-to-end test exists that upgrades a simulated on-prem cluster with zero accepted customer errors and validates rollback path
notes: Architectural sketch: coordinator -> cohort-controller -> step-runners (upgrade, migrate, validate) -> telemetry sink. Step-runners run small idempotent tasks and record checkpoints.

Compatibility model: semantic-major policy + component capability matrix. Version pins honor LTS channels; if a requested version conflicts, Stitch Runner will compute the minimal compatible variant or block with remediation steps.
Rollback strategy: keep prior images/configs in a readonly artifact store and run reverse steps; for DB backfills use reversible checkpoints and apply compensating migrations when necessary.
Operator UX: provide 'pause', 'advance', and 'abort' controls in Console with RBAC gate checks; CLI supports dry-run and signed approvals for regulated customers.
Next steps: finish non-flaky simulation tests, complete security review for CLI secrets, wire Console rollout UI hooks, and schedule customer beta with two early adopter accounts.
